_comment: Non-English spellings of the SAME high-frequency people already listed in gazetteer_names.json (English), each paired with the SAME short_form already used there — this is what makes a Chinese/Russian/French/etc. mention of this person resolve to the identical canonical token entity_tokens() already emits for the English mention, closing the cross-lingual same-event-matching gap found 2026-09-06. zh_hans/zh_hant/fr/de entries below are exact-match (these languages don't inflect personal names, or China/Breaks' own gazetteer already only needs the bare form) — see 'inflected_stems' for ru/pl, which is a SEPARATE, prefix-matched list because Russian/Polish grammatical case endings (e.g. Russian instrumental 'Путиным', Polish genitive 'Trumpa') change the tail of the word, so an exact-string list would silently miss every declined mention in real running text (confirmed 2026-09-06: real log data had 'Witkoffem'/'Zełenskiego'/'Trumpa', none of which matched the exact nominative forms first tried). fa (Persian) deliberately left empty everywhere — no independently-verified transliteration source, do not fill in without one. Chinese (zh_hans/zh_hant) matching additionally requires a CJK word-segmentation step before these patterns can ever fire on real running text — see event_identity.py's own note on this; not yet wired in as of this file's last edit.

roles._comment: Reference only — NOT consumed by entity_tokens()/event matching. English-language role tag per person, for editorial/prompt reference.
roles.Xi Jinping: President of the PRC / CCP General Secretary
roles.JD Vance: Vice President of the United States
roles.Keir Starmer: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

inflected_stems._comment: [stem, short_form] pairs matched as a REGEX PREFIX (^stem), not exact strings — for Russian/Polish, whose grammatical case endings get appended to a name's stem (Putin -> Путина/Путину/Путиным/Путине; Trump -> Trumpa/Trumpowi/Trumpem). A single stem entry covers every declined form without needing to enumerate all 6 Russian / 7 Polish cases by hand. Known residual gap: this only helps when the case ending is ADDED to the stem, not when the final vowel itself changes (e.g. a Polish '-o' ending name like Rubio might become 'Rubia' in genitive, which this stem form won't catch) — narrower than a real morphological analyzer, but covers the common consonant-stem case that caused the real misses found 2026-09-06 (Witkoffem, Zełenskiego, Trumpa all match their stems below).

gpe_places._comment: Chinese names for the countries/regions/cities that actually recur in this feed's real coverage (2026-09-07) — NOT an exhaustive gazetteer, same 'attack real high-frequency misses first' philosophy as the PERSON lists above. Root problem this closes: entity_tokens() has ZERO real GPE/place recognition for Chinese text at all — en_core_web_sm's statistical NER has never seen Chinese script, so even after jieba segmentation, a Chinese place name is just an unrecognized token, never tagged GPE (confirmed 2026-09-07: a real Nepal/Tibet flood article and a real 'Freedom Edge' US-Japan-Korea drill article both produced zero GPE tokens from their Chinese versions, while their English equivalents produced 'nepal'/'tibet'/'korea'/'japan'/'us' etc. fine). Each entry's second field is a SPACE-SEPARATED string of every English alias this codebase's own NER commonly produces for that place (e.g. 'United States' and 'U.S.' tokenize to different word sets) — entity_tokens() runs this whole alias string through the same _TOKEN_RE tokenizer already used for PERSON short_forms, so listing multiple aliases in one string adds ALL of their tokens at once, maximizing the chance of a real overlap regardless of which form the English article actually used. Russian entries added 2026-09-07 after a chinabreaks_events audit found an event with completely EMPTY seed_entities — a Russian article about a Russia-North Korea bridge (naming 'КНДР' and 'Приморье') produced zero GPE tokens since this gazetteer previously only covered Chinese script. verify_compatibility()'s own 'if not core: return COMPATIBLE' fail-open default means an event with an empty core fingerprint blindly accepts ANY later candidate compared against it, regardless of real relevance — Приморье/Владивосток specifically included because those are the exact place names the real miss involved, not just the standard country-list pattern.

joint_mentions._comment: Chinese-media shorthand that fuses TWO leaders' surnames into one compound term for their summit/meeting (e.g. '川習會' = Chuan[Trump]+Xi+meeting = 'the Trump-Xi summit') — a real production miss found 2026-09-07: 'news.ltn.com.tw's own report on the same Trump-Xi AI-guardrails talks asia.nikkei.com covered got NO_OVERLAP because jieba's default dictionary mis-split '透過川習會' into '透'+'過川習'+'會', and even correctly segmented, this compound isn't any SINGLE registered PERSON name, so it could never match a one-person short_form lookup. Each entry maps the compound to the LIST of short_forms of every person it names (not one) — entity_tokens() emits ALL of them when this exact compound is matched, same as if both individual names had appeared separately. Every compound is also registered as a jieba word (see _register_cjk_gazetteer_words) so it survives segmentation as one unit instead of being split apart. Starting list only — the common 'X+Y+會/会' pattern recurs constantly in Chinese/Taiwanese headlines for whichever two leaders are meeting, so expand this as real ones are found missing, same as the rest of this file.

role_terms_reference._comment: Multilingual glossary of the 6 role categories, per user's request — NOT wired into entity_tokens()/matching (a bare role word like '外交部长' shared between two articles about two different foreign ministers would cause false same-event merges if used as a matching token; GPT-4o-mini already understands these roles natively in every language when scoring/writing, so this table's real use is as an editorial/human reference, or a future building block if a different feature needs it). fa left empty, no verified source.
